blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — The Senate impeachment court said on Friday that former Sen. Antonio Trillanes IV has the right to free speech, but his statements will not be the senator-judges’ basis to either convict or acquit Vice President Sara Duterte. Impeachment court spokesperson Atty. Reginald Tongol made the assertion shortly after Trillanes held a press conference. The former senator earlier held a media briefing presenting supposed evidence on Duterte’s alleged ill-gotten wealth had he not been withdrawn as a witness in the trial. “They are free to exhaust their freedom of speech because that is part of our democracy,” Tongol began.
